priceSnapshot.note: THE DAY BITCOIN WAS HANDED EVERYTHING AND DID NOTHING WITH IT. The completed 2026-07-30 UTC daily candle is a genuine up day - open 63,999.9, high 65,152.4, low 63,611.0, close 64,781.7, +1.25% on the previous close of 63,983.3 - and on any normal tape that would read well. It does not read well in context. Over the same session the dollar index broke BELOW 100 to 99.999, down 0.88% and a fresh six-week low; QQQ closed +3.30% at 683.55 and the Nasdaq-100 cash index +3.70%; the S&P proxy closed +1.77%; JPXN closed +3.96%; the 10-year sat still at 4.68%; and the June core PCE print that capped this morning's confidence cleared benign. A falling dollar, stable yields, and a 3.7% melt-up in tech is the single friendliest combination BTC has been offered all week, and BTC answered with 1.25% and a rejected high. Since the midday snapshot at 64,941.6 price has done nothing at all: high 65,075.0, low 64,670.2, now 64,763.2, a net -0.27% across six and a half hours. The two things that changed underneath are both cautionary. First, spot is back BELOW the daily EMA50 at 64,935.52 after spending midday sitting nine dollars under it - the gate has now rejected price twice in one session. Second, the crypto-native sentiment gauge went the WRONG way on an up day: Fear & Greed printed 25 (Extreme Fear) at 00:00Z against 28 at midday. Equities are euphoric and crypto is not participating in the mood, which is usually a positioning story rather than a macro one.

decisionBox.changed: Stance moves ADD -> REDUCE. Bias tilt flips bullish -> bearish. Confidence 6.00 -> 5.50. Probabilities 35/45/20 -> 28/45/27. Four things changed since 12:50 COT, and the first one is the whole argument: (1) NON-CONFIRMATION. Midday's ADD was taken on the thesis that a cleared PCE print plus a six-week-low dollar would let BTC convert the 65,000 break. The macro delivered more than midday assumed - DXY went through 100 to 99.999, QQQ closed +3.30%, the Nasdaq-100 cash index +3.70% - and BTC is 0.27% LOWER than when the trade was put on. An asset that will not go up on its best possible news is telling you where the marginal bid is. (2) THE DAILY EMA50 REJECTED PRICE AGAIN. Spot is 64,763.2 against 64,935.52; the 65,075.0 high failed under it and the 65,152.4 day high failed under it. Two rejections at the same gate in one session. (3) THE LIQUIDITY PULL INVERTED. Midday read the pull as UP with the heaviest measured cluster $183 above spot. The CoinGlass 48h heatmap read this run puts the heaviest nearby band BELOW, at 64,323.64 (414.25K) against 65,600.92 (271.19K) above - a 53% skew toward the downside magnet. (4) SENTIMENT DIVERGED. Fear & Greed fell 28 -> 25 (Extreme Fear) on a day the equity tape ripped. The REDUCE itself is deliberately small - roughly a tenth of the spot core - and it does double duty: it de-risks the overnight gap on a bearish tilt, and it funds the 30 USDT cost-of-living charge that lands on 2026-08-01 without a forced sale at whatever price happens to print then.

overnightRisk: The next report is at ~02:00 COT and then the tape runs unattended until roughly 06:50 COT - six and a half hours of the thinnest liquidity of the day, with no US cash market and no Asian equity open until the back half of the window. Four specific things make this particular night worth a resting stop. FIRST, the liquidation geography is stacked against a drift lower. The heaviest measured band near spot is BELOW at $64,323.64 (414.25K leverage reading), and behind it sit $63,826.92 (218.39K) and a second heavy shelf at $63,330.20 (370.79K). A slow overnight bleed of 0.7% reaches the first magnet; 2.2% reaches the second heavy one. In thin books, magnets get tagged. SECOND, the trigger for that bleed is already identifiable: BTC spent the entire US session refusing to price a six-week-low dollar and a +3.70% Nasdaq-100. If Asia opens and the dollar simply stops falling, the one prop under this level goes away and there is nothing underneath but the shelf. THIRD, the yen. USDJPY fell 2.23% to 159.748 today; a disorderly extension of that move is the classic overnight carry-unwind channel into crypto, and it happens in the exact hours nobody is watching. FOURTH, month-end. This is the last session of July; the 2026-07-31 UTC candle is a month-end close, and month-end rebalancing flows are mechanical, price-insensitive, and land in the London hours inside this gap. Against all of that, the honest counterweight: the 4H structure is genuinely intact - price is above the 4H EMA20 (64,431), EMA50 (64,494), EMA100 (64,384) and EMA200 (63,968), the 4H MACD line is 56.28 above a signal of -66.10 with a +122.38 histogram, and the 64,610-64,750 shelf that midday named was tested at 64,670.2 tonight and held. The base case is still a quiet range. The stop at $63,200 is not a forecast; it is sized one Wilder ATR-14 (1,505.83, or 2.33%) below spot and placed BELOW the $63,330 magnet on purpose, so that a normal night cannot reach it and only a real break can.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is DOWN, and unlike midday's UP call this one is not close. The heaviest band within 1% of spot is 64,323.64 at 414.25K, against 65,600.92 at 271.19K above - a 53% skew, with the downside band also sitting half the distance away (0.68% below versus 1.29% above). The header numbers add a second, softer downside argument: 24h liquidations collapsed 54.88% to $176.2M while open interest ROSE 3.20% to $114.4B. Positions are being added, not closed, and almost nobody is being forced out - that is a market with plenty of unspent fuel and no recent flush, which is the setup that makes a magnet reachable rather than one that has already been consumed. The honest case against reading too much into it: the 24h long/short split is 50.75%/49.25%, a ratio of 1.03, which is as close to neutral as this gauge gets and nothing like the crowded-long 1.26-1.81 readings of the past three days. A balanced book cuts both ways - there is no trapped-long overhang to cascade, but there are also no trapped shorts left to squeeze. Read the two bands as the edges of the overnight range and let price choose.
